stories.headline: OpenAI says two API settings tripled GPT-5.6 Sol's ARC-AGI-3 score; ARC Prize pushes back

key_facts.fact: In a July 29 post, OpenAI said turning on two API settings it already uses in ChatGPT and Codex — retained reasoning and compaction — tripled GPT-5.6 Sol's ARC-AGI-3 score on the public task set and cut output tokens by 6x
key_facts.excerpt: In the case of ARC-AGI-3, we discovered that turning on two API settings we use in ChatGPT and Codex—retained reasoning and compaction—tripled scores and cut output tokens by 6x on the public task set.

key_facts.fact: With the official ARC-AGI-3 harness GPT-5.6 Sol scored 13.3% on the public set; reimplemented on OpenAI's Responses API with retained reasoning and compaction it scored 38.3%, using roughly six times fewer output tokens per game
key_facts.excerpt: With the official ARC-AGI-3 harness, GPT-5.6 Sol scored 13.3% on the public task set. Using OpenAI's Responses API with retained reasoning and compaction turned on, the same model scored 38.3%, while using roughly six times fewer output tokens per game.

key_facts.fact: The 38.3% figure would beat Anthropic's Claude Opus 5 at 30.2%; in ARC's official harness GPT-5.6 Sol had scored just 7.8% because reasoning is discarded after each action
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI is now showing that GPT-5.6 Sol hits 38.3 percent with two API settings, beating Opus 5's 30.2 percent... In the official harness, GPT-5.6 Sol scored just 7.8 percent because the model's reasoning gets discarded after each action.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI blamed the generic harness: private reasoning was thrown away after every action, and rolling truncation dropped the oldest context once the conversation passed 175,000 characters
key_facts.excerpt: After every action the agent took, its private reasoning was thrown away... the harness used rolling truncation, discarding the oldest parts of the conversation once it grew past 175,000 characters

key_facts.fact: ARC Prize called the finding 'a real and useful result' but said its verified scores deliberately use a 'no harness' approach with client-side conversation state so all providers are compared under the same observations, prompt and action limits
key_facts.excerpt: ARC's verified scores use a "no harness" approach to avoid accidental or intentional developer-aware targeting and to fairly compare scores across all providers... Conversation state is managed client-side using the industry-wide standard interface for LLMs (the OpenAI-style completions API).

key_facts.fact: ARC Prize said it is working with several industry labs, including OpenAI, on how to incorporate server-side state management into its verified testing setup
key_facts.excerpt: we're actively working with several industry labs, including OpenAI, to figure out how to best incorporate these server-side state management findings into our verified testing setup while remaining fair and consistent across providers.

stories.headline: EU set to put ChatGPT under its strictest platform rules as a 'very large online platform'

key_facts.fact: The European Commission will designate OpenAI's ChatGPT and Roblox as 'very large online platforms' under the Digital Services Act after both passed 45 million monthly users in the bloc, with the move set to come as soon as August
key_facts.excerpt: The EU's executive arm will designate the two US technology companies as "very large online platforms" (VLOPs) in line with the Digital Services Act (DSA), a person familiar with the matter said. The designation is set to come as soon as August

key_facts.fact: VLOPs must file transparency reports, detail risk mitigation plans and pay an annual fee to the Commission; breaches carry fines of up to 6% of annual global sales
key_facts.excerpt: The "VLOPs"... must also file transparency reports, detail risk mitigation plans and pay an annual fee to the European Commission. Companies that breach the DSA risk fines of as much as 6 per cent of their annual global sales.

key_facts.fact: Within four months of designation the companies must set up a contact point for authorities and users, publish user-friendly terms, and be transparent about advertising, recommendation systems and content moderation decisions
key_facts.excerpt: Within four months of being officially designation as a VLOP, they will have to establish a point of contact for authorities and users, launch user-friendly terms and conditions, as well as be transparent when it comes to their advertising, recommendation systems and content moderation decisions.

key_facts.fact: Designated platforms must run annual audits, share data with the Commission and give vetted researchers access, and assess systemic risks including illegal content and electoral processes
key_facts.excerpt: VLOPs are required to establish an internal compliance process, be audited every year... share their data with the European Commission and allow vetted researchers to access it, as well.

key_facts.fact: ChatGPT crossed 120 million monthly users in Europe last year; 21 platforms including X, Amazon, Apple, Microsoft, LinkedIn and TikTok are already subject to the rules
key_facts.excerpt: 21 platforms in the bloc, including X, Amazon, Apple, Microsoft, LinkedIn and TikTok, are already subject to these regulations since the DSA's enforcement in early 2024... ChatGPT crossed 120m monthly users in Europe last year.

stories.headline: EU opens bidding for seven AI gigafactories, aiming to mobilise 30 billion euros

key_facts.fact: The European Commission published the long-delayed call for tenders on Thursday, a 5 billion euro EU procurement notice covering a multi-site, multi-country design for seven AI gigafactories
key_facts.excerpt: The EU published a long-awaited call-for-tender to build flagship AI compute infrastructure on Thursday – with a €5 billion EU funding procurement notice covering a multi-site, multi-country design for seven AI gigafactories.

key_facts.fact: Total investment for the seven sites is put at 30 billion euros: 5 billion from the EU, 5 billion from member states and 20 billion from private investors; the call closes on 12 November
key_facts.excerpt: The total investment for seven gigafactories will amount to €30 billion: €5 billion from the EU, €5 billion from EU countries and €20 billion from private investors... The call for tenders is due to close on 12 November.

key_facts.fact: Applicants must show measures to mitigate 'vendor lock-in', a provision aimed at limiting Nvidia's dominance in data center AI chips, with low-scoring consortia facing disqualification
key_facts.excerpt: The call for proposals includes a measure aimed at limiting Nvidia's dominance in AI chips for data centres: Applicants must demonstrate measures applied to mitigate "vendor lock-in", with low-scoring consortia facing disqualification.

key_facts.fact: Funding runs through the EuroHPC Joint Undertaking with 18 member states, in two strands worth up to 500 million euros and up to 1 billion euros per facility; award decisions are expected in early 2027
key_facts.excerpt: Funding is to be channelled through the European High Performance Computing Joint Undertaking (EuroHPC JU). key_facts.fact: The Commission expanded the plan from four or five sites to up to seven after 76 expressions of interest covering 60 sites in 16 member states; construction is to start in early 2027 and the facilities to be operational by mid-2028
key_facts.excerpt: the Commission has expanded its initial scope from four or five gigafactories to up to seven... The successful projects are expected to begin physical construction of the gigafactories at the start of 2027, with facilities due to become operational by mid-2028.

key_facts.fact: Each gigafactory is to house at least 100,000 cutting-edge AI chips, about four times more powerful than data centers now running in the EU, whose current compute would more than double once the seven sites come online
key_facts.excerpt: Firms can now bid for contracts to build gigafactories that are planned to have at least 100,000 cutting-edge AI chips, making them roughly four times more powerful than the data centres currently running in the EU.

key_facts.excerpt: Capital expenditures were $41 billion in the quarter; roughly two-thirds went toward short-lived assets, primarily CPUs and GPUs, while finance leases totaled $5.6 billion.

key_facts.excerpt: Microsoft accelerated its AI infrastructure expansion in fiscal 2026, adding 88 data centers during the year, another 1 GW of capacity in the fourth quarter, and nearly $116 billion in property and equipment spending... Property and equipment increased to $313.1 billion from $205.0 billion a year earlier

key_facts.fact: Microsoft will now spread long-term data center leases over 25 years instead of 15, lowering reported capex: it guided to about $175 billion for calendar 2026 versus its own prior $190 billion estimate, and more than $50 billion in the current quarter, while saying spending plans are unchanged
key_facts.excerpt: Microsoft also said it would now spread long-term leases on data centers over 25 years rather than 15, which has the effect of lowering its annual reported capital expenditures. stories.headline: US launches 'heavy wave' of strikes on dozens of IRGC targets in Iran; Guard vows to punish

key_facts.fact: US Central Command said it completed a 'heavy wave of strikes against Iran' as of 10pm ET on Wednesday July 29 (02:00 GMT July 30), after a five-night pause in strikes.
key_facts.excerpt: The US military's Central Command (CENTCOM) said it had 'successfully completed a heavy wave of strikes against Iran' as of 10pm ET on Wednesday (02:00 GMT on Thursday).

key_facts.fact: The strikes began at 8pm ET and ran two hours, hitting dozens of Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps targets including military command centres, missile and drone facilities, coastal surveillance and defence sites, and maritime capabilities.
key_facts.excerpt: "CENTCOM assets struck dozens of Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) targets in Iran, including military command centres, missile and drone facilities, coastal surveillance and defence sites, and maritime capabilities," the US Central Command said.

key_facts.fact: CENTCOM framed the operation as retaliation for Iran's attempted missile attack on US forces at a base in Jordan a day earlier; Jordan's army said it intercepted five Iranian missiles.
key_facts.excerpt: The U.S. military said early Thursday it had completed "a heavy wave of strikes against Iran" conducted in response to an earlier Iranian missile attack on a U.S. base in Jordan.

key_facts.fact: Iranian media reported three civilians killed in the latest strikes, and the IRGC said three of its personnel were killed.
key_facts.excerpt: Iranian media reported that three civilians were killed in the latest strikes. Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) also said three of its personnel were killed in a US missile attack.

key_facts.fact: On Thursday the Revolutionary Guard said it 'will punish the aggressor today' and warned that countries helping the US would receive a 'harsh response', while insisting it keeps 'full control' of the Strait of Hormuz.
key_facts.excerpt: The US attacks began at 8 p.m. ET on Wednesday (0000 GMT on Thursday) and ended at 10 p.m. ET (0200 GMT on Thursday), according to CENTCOM.

key_facts.fact: Trump telegraphed the retaliation hours earlier, telling Fox News: 'We'll be hitting them hard ... We are going to beat the effing s out of them.'
key_facts.excerpt: Ahead of the latest strikes, US President Trump told Fox News: "We'll be hitting them hard ... We are going to beat the 'effing s' out of them."

key_facts.fact: Saudi Arabia's defence minister met US Vice-President JD Vance to urge the administration not to escalate further by attacking Yemen's Houthis or carrying out more strikes in Iraq.
key_facts.excerpt: After the joint attacks, Saudi Arabia's defence minister met with US Vice-President JD Vance to urge the Trump administration not to escalate the conflict further by attacking Yemen's Houthis or by carrying out additional strikes in Iraq, two sources told the Reuters news agency.

stories.headline: Fed holds rates at 3.5%-3.75% in 9-3 vote, with three officials dissenting in favor of a hike

key_facts.fact: The FOMC voted 9-3 on July 29 to keep the federal funds target range at 3-1/2 to 3-3/4 percent, the fifth consecutive hold.
key_facts.excerpt: The Federal Open Market Committee approved the following statement for release by a 9 – 3 vote: The Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 3-1/2 to 3-3/4 percent.

key_facts.fact: Cleveland's Beth Hammack, Minneapolis' Neel Kashkari and Dallas' Lorie Logan dissented, preferring a quarter-point increase.
key_facts.excerpt: Voting against the monetary policy action were Beth M. Hammack, Neel Kashkari, and Lorie K. Logan, who preferred to raise the target range for the federal funds rate by 1/4 percentage point at this meeting.

key_facts.fact: It was the first time three voters dissented since September 2016.
key_facts.excerpt: July's decision marks the first time 3 voters dissented since 2016... a trio of policymakers dissented in favor of a hike – the most seen since September 2016.

key_facts.fact: The statement said economic activity is expanding at a solid pace 'despite elevated uncertainty that owes, in part, to the conflict in the Middle East', and that inflation remains elevated relative to the 2% goal partly because of energy supply shocks.
key_facts.excerpt: The FOMC noted that "economic activity is expanding at a solid pace despite elevated uncertainty that owes, in part, to the conflict in the Middle East." Policymakers noted that inflation remains above the Fed's 2% goal, in part because of supply shocks driving price increases in sectors such as energy.

key_facts.fact: Chairman Kevin Warsh, in his second meeting, said 'I asked for a good family fight and I got one' and reiterated there is no soft or implicit inflation target above 2%.
key_facts.excerpt: Let me reiterate: There is no soft inflation target, there is no soft implicit target —not on this Committee's watch. There is only a target, and it is 2 percent.

key_facts.fact: After the decision, CME FedWatch showed a 57.2% probability of a 25-basis-point hike at the September 15-16 meeting.
key_facts.excerpt: The CME FedWatch tool shows a 41.9% chance the Fed will leave rates at their current level in September, up from 24% a day ago. It also shows a 57.2% probability of a 25-basis-point rate hike in September.

key_facts.fact: The last change to rates was a quarter-point cut in December 2025; inflation has run above the Fed's 2% target for more than five years.
key_facts.excerpt: The last time Fed officials voted to change interest rates was in December 2025, when it reduced its key rate by 0.25 percentage points.

stories.headline: Russia fires 74 missiles and 284 drones at Ukraine; a Russian missile appears to land in Poland

key_facts.fact: Russia launched more than 70 missiles, many of them ballistic, and more than 280 attack drones overnight into July 30, hitting Kyiv plus nine other regions from Lviv to Kharkiv.
key_facts.excerpt: Russia launched more than 70 missiles and about 280 drones, Zelensky said in a statement on the Telegram app.

key_facts.fact: Ukraine's air force said it downed 55 missiles and 265 drones but only one of nine ballistic missiles; 11 missiles and 17 drones hit targets at 20 locations.
key_facts.excerpt: Air defence units shot down 55 missiles and 265 drones but only one of nine ballistic missiles, Ukraine's air force said, adding that 11 missiles and 17 drones hit targets at 20 locations.

key_facts.fact: Zelensky put the toll at least eight dead including three children; Reuters later reported at least 13 killed across Ukraine.
key_facts.excerpt: Russian air strikes killed at least 13 people in Ukraine on Thursday, including one in Kyiv, in attacks extending as far as the western city of Lviv, forcing neighboring Poland to scramble fighter jets to secure its airspace.

key_facts.fact: The deadliest strike hit the village of Radushne near Kryvyi Rih, where an Iskander-M ballistic missile destroyed a family's home, killing six including a 6-year-old girl and boys aged 11 and 17.
key_facts.excerpt: Russian forces struck the home of a large family in the village of Radushne with a ballistic missile. Six people were killed, including the parents and three children — a six-year-old girl and two boys aged 11 and 17.

key_facts.fact: In Lviv, missiles damaged more than 20 residential buildings, a school and two kindergartens, injuring at least 26 people.
key_facts.excerpt: A missile strike on Lviv injured at least 26 people... More than 20 residential buildings were damaged citywide, along with a school and two kindergartens.

key_facts.fact: Poland scrambled an F-16 and a helicopter after detecting an unidentified object; a 10-metre crater and debris were found in the Lublin region, and Prime Minister Donald Tusk said 'it looks like it was a Russian missile'.
key_facts.excerpt: Following an ongoing investigation into the source of a ten-metre crater found in Poland on Thursday, the Polish prime minister has said: "It looks like it was a Russian missile, but we don't have a hundred per cent certainty exactly what kind of missile."

key_facts.fact: Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said the object that crossed into Poland was a Russian Kh-101 cruise missile, calling it a violation of NATO airspace; the attack came as Zelensky returned from Washington saying Trump agreed to license Patriot missiles for Ukraine.
key_facts.excerpt: Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha alleged on X that the object that crossed into Poland was a Russian Kh-101 cruise missile.

key_facts.fact: Russia's Defense Ministry said it struck military facilities from Kyiv to Lviv and Dnipropetrovsk as well as three cargo ships; a Wildberries warehouse in Penza caught fire after a Ukrainian drone attack.
key_facts.excerpt: Russia's defence ministry said on July 30 its forces struck what it called military facilities across Ukraine, from Kyiv to Lviv and Dnipropetrovsk, as well as three cargo ships... a warehouse of Russian top online retailer Wildberries caught fire in the western city of Penza after a Ukrainian drone attack.

stories.headline: FDA panel votes 9-3 against Capricor's cell therapy for Duchenne muscular dystrophy

key_facts.fact: The FDA's Cellular, Tissue, and Gene Therapies Advisory Committee voted 9-3 on Wednesday July 29 against deramiocel, Capricor Therapeutics' cell therapy for Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
key_facts.excerpt: The agency's Cellular, Tissue, and Gene Therapies Advisory Committee voted 9-3 against the drug on Wednesday, with some panelists offering moderate support.

key_facts.fact: The vote sided with FDA reviewers who said deramiocel failed to show significant efficacy; that review triggered a more than 60% slide in Capricor's stock on Monday.
key_facts.excerpt: the committee's vote sided with FDA reviewers who had maintained deramiocel had failed to show significant efficacy. That analysis triggered a slide of more than 60% in Capricor's stock price on Monday.

key_facts.fact: The agency's acting biologics director Karim Mikhail said no final decision has been made and the FDA has until Aug. 22 to approve or reject the therapy; the FDA first rejected it in July 2025.
key_facts.excerpt: he noted, no final decision has been made, and the agency has until Aug. 22 to approve or reject the drug. The FDA first rejected the drug in July 2025 but later granted Capricor the chance to make its case.

key_facts.fact: The Lancet simultaneously published Capricor's HOPE-3 results, which the company said provide 'external validation' of the trial's positive findings.
key_facts.excerpt: As the meeting took shape, The Lancet simultaneously published Capricor's results from HOPE-3, a step that the company said provides "external validation" of the positive findings from the trial.

key_facts.fact: Capricor argues the FDA's briefing materials relied on an obsolete statistical analysis plan (SAP version 1.1) rather than the final SAP 3.0 finalized before unblinding, and says HOPE-3 hit its primary endpoint PUL 2.0 with statistical significance.
key_facts.excerpt: the post-hoc analyses in the FDA's briefing materials rely on SAP version 1.1, an unsigned incomplete internal draft which became obsolete... The Phase 3 HOPE-3 results demonstrate a statistically significant benefit on the primary endpoint, PUL 2.0.

stories.headline: SpaceX wins $1.6B in Space Force orders for 18 Falcon 9 launches of military sensing satellites

key_facts.fact: The US Space Force awarded SpaceX two launch task orders worth $1.6 billion, the largest publicly announced batch of missions yet under the National Security Space Launch Phase 3 program.
key_facts.excerpt: The U.S. Space Force awarded SpaceX two launch task orders worth $1.6 billion to deploy military satellite constellations, marking the largest publicly announced batch of missions yet under the National Security Space Launch Phase 3 program.

key_facts.fact: The award covers 18 Falcon 9 launches from Vandenberg Space Force Base through the end of 2027 in support of the Space Based Sensing and Targeting portfolio.
key_facts.excerpt: The award covers 18 Falcon 9 launches from Vandenberg Space Force Base in California through the end of 2027 in support of the Space Based Sensing and Targeting portfolio.

key_facts.fact: It is the largest disclosed order under NSSL Phase 3 Lane 1, and follows the Space Force's decision earlier in July to raise that contract's ceiling to $17 billion from $5.6 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: The contract also follows the Space Force's decision earlier this month to raise the Phase 3 Lane 1 contract ceiling to $17 billion from $5.6 billion, reflecting expectations that military launch demand will grow substantially faster than originally anticipated.

key_facts.fact: Completing 18 launches by end-2027 implies roughly one mission a month from Vandenberg; seven companies hold Lane 1 positions but SpaceX is the only one with the cadence and West Coast infrastructure to support it.
key_facts.excerpt: Completing 18 launches by the end of 2027 will require a sustained campaign averaging roughly one mission a month from Vandenberg... For now, SpaceX remains the only company with the combination of launch frequency, operational Falcon 9 rockets and West Coast infrastructure needed to support a campaign of this scale.

key_facts.fact: Separately, SpaceX launched the classified NROL-95 payload for the National Reconnaissance Office from Cape Canaveral at 3:09 a.m. ET on July 30, the NRO's fourth launch of 2026 and its third Falcon 9 mission under NSSL Phase 2.
key_facts.excerpt: The NROL-95 mission will launch onboard a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket flying from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station. Liftoff from Space Launch Complex 40 is scheduled for 3:10 a.m. EDT (0710 UTC).

key_facts.fact: With Blue Origin and ULA offline due to launch-system problems, SpaceX is currently the only provider flying national security payloads from the Cape.
key_facts.excerpt: With Blue Origin and ULA offline due to problems with their launch systems, that leaves SpaceX as the only game in town.
